description: A practical guide to yoga in Rishikesh: why the town is called the yoga capital of the world, traditional ashrams such as Parmarth Niketan and the Sivananda Ashram, schools around Tapovan and Lakshman Jhula, drop-in classes, retreats and 200-hour teacher training, the International Yoga Festival, the Beatles Ashram, where to stay, the best season and how to choose a course.
dek: Rishikesh draws yoga students from all over the world to its ashrams and schools on the banks of the Ganga.

intro: Rishikesh, where the Ganga leaves the Himalayan foothills, has been a place of retreat for sages for centuries. In the 20th century ashrams such as the Sivananda Ashram (Divine Life Society) made it a centre for yoga, and the Beatles' stay in 1968 at the ashram of Maharishi Mahesh Yogi brought international attention.

Today the town has hundreds of ashrams, schools and studios, from traditional institutions with daily routines to modern schools running teacher-training courses. Rishikesh is a vegetarian, alcohol-free town, which suits a retreat.
quickAnswer: Rishikesh is known as the yoga capital of the world, with traditional ashrams such as Parmarth Niketan and the Sivananda Ashram and many schools around Tapovan and Lakshman Jhula. Visitors can join drop-in classes, week-long retreats or 200-hour teacher-training courses of about four weeks. The International Yoga Festival is held at Parmarth Niketan each March. September to November and February to April are the best seasons.
takeaways: Choose between drop-in classes, short retreats and teacher-training courses.
Parmarth Niketan and the Sivananda Ashram are among the oldest and best-known ashrams.
Most schools cluster around Tapovan, Lakshman Jhula and Ram Jhula.
The International Yoga Festival is held at Parmarth Niketan each March.

items.name: Parmarth Niketan
body: A large ashram on the Ganga at Swarg Ashram, known for its evening Ganga Aarti and for hosting the International Yoga Festival.

sections.heading: How to choose a school
list: Look at the teachers' training and experience, class sizes and the daily schedule.
For teacher training, check the course hours, syllabus and any external registration the school offers.
Visit for a drop-in class before committing to a long course.
Read recent independent reviews, and be wary of prices far below the norm.
Book directly with the school or ashram.

sections.heading: Etiquette
list: Dress modestly in the town and at the ghats; practice clothes are fine inside schools.
Remove shoes before entering ashram halls and temples.
Rishikesh is vegetarian and alcohol-free; respect the rule.
Keep noise down at the ghats during the aarti and meditation.

sections.heading: When to go
list: September to November: clear weather after the monsoon; the busiest season for courses.
February to April: pleasant, with the International Yoga Festival in March.
December and January: cold mornings and evenings; fewer students.
May and June: hot. July and August: monsoon rain, and river activities pause.

sections.heading: Where to stay
list: Ashrams: simple rooms with a daily routine and set meal times.
Tapovan and Lakshman Jhula: guesthouses and hotels close to schools.
Near Ram Jhula and Swarg Ashram: close to Parmarth Niketan and the ghats.
Riverside resorts upstream for more comfort and quiet.

sections.heading: Beyond yoga
list: The evening Ganga Aarti at Triveni Ghat and Parmarth Niketan.
Neelkanth Mahadev temple in the hills above the town.
Haridwar's Har ki Pauri, about an hour away.
Rafting on the Ganga from September to June, when permitted.

safety: Check a centre's teachers, daily schedule, rules and reviews before booking; no retreat can promise a particular spiritual or health outcome, and people with medical conditions should take advice before intensive practice.
Swim only at designated spots; the Ganga's current is strong.
Keep valuables secure in busy areas around the bridges.
packing: A shawl or warm layer for early mornings
Modest clothes for ashrams and ghats

faqs.q: Why is Rishikesh called the yoga capital of the world?
faqs.a: Because of its long tradition of ashrams and sages and the large number of yoga schools and ashrams in the town today.

faqs.q: How long is yoga teacher training in Rishikesh?
faqs.a: A 200-hour course usually takes about four weeks.

faqs.q: When is the International Yoga Festival in Rishikesh?
Can beginners do yoga in Rishikesh?
faqs.a: Yes. Drop-in classes and beginner courses are widely available.

faqs.q: Is Rishikesh safe for solo travellers?
faqs.a: It is popular with solo travellers; take usual precautions and stay in registered accommodation.

faqs.q: What is the best time for yoga in Rishikesh?
faqs.a: September to November and February to April.
